card.name: assistantStatus
card.title: Assistant status
card.subtitle: Two switches, and they do different things. The first stops the assistant from answering at all. The second only hides it from your storefront.

input-field.name: widgetEnabled
input-field.label: Show the assistant in your storefront
input-field.helpText: Turn this off to remove the assistant from your shop pages while leaving it running. The chat endpoint stays reachable, so your own interface built against it keeps working — that is the difference between this switch and the one above. The assistant also hides itself when no model is configured.

card.name: languageModel
card.title: Language model
card.subtitle: The assistant cannot answer anything until a model is set here.

input-field.name: llmBaseUrl
input-field.label: OpenAI-compatible base URL
input-field.helpText: Any OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint (Azure, OpenRouter, a local model). The URL is checked on every request to make sure it points outside your own network; a private or loopback address is rejected.

input-field.name: llmModel
input-field.label: Model
input-field.helpText: The assistant is inert until this is set. Choose a model that handles tool calling reliably — a weak model here reads to your shoppers as a bad product, not as a configuration choice.

input-field.name: llmApiKey
input-field.label: API key
input-field.helpText: Prefer an environment variable. Shopware's settings have no real secret storage, so a key entered here can be read by anyone with config access and ends up in database backups.

card.name: voiceAndScope
card.title: Voice and catalogue scope
card.subtitle: Anything listed here is hidden from the assistant entirely: it is never looked up, so it cannot be mentioned, recommended or added to a cart.

input-field.name: agentVoice
input-field.label: Agent voice
input-field.placeholder: Warm and concise. Speak like a knowledgeable shop assistant, not a salesperson. Never oversell — if something is not a good fit, say so.
input-field.helpText: Tone and personality only. Nothing written here can give the assistant a new ability: what it is allowed to do is decided by the switches in this form, never by instructions in this box.

input-field.name: blockedProducts
input-field.label: Blocked product IDs
input-field.helpText: One ID per line. Hides this product. Blocking a product that has variants hides all of them, so you do not have to list each colour or size. Blocked products never reach the model and can never appear in a reply — this filters what gets looked up rather than asking the model to behave, so it cannot be talked around.

input-field.name: blockedCategories
input-field.label: Blocked category IDs
input-field.helpText: One ID per line. Hides everything in this category and everything below it. Same guarantee as blocked products.

card.name: limits
card.title: Limits
card.subtitle: Everything here is unlimited unless you set a number. Leave a field at 0 and no limit applies.

input-field.name: enableAddToCart
input-field.label: Let the assistant add items to the cart
input-field.helpText: When off, the add-to-cart tool is never built, so the model cannot see it and cannot call it. Add buttons disappear from the assistant's product cards too.

input-field.name: maxItemQuantity
input-field.label: Most units of one item the assistant may add
input-field.helpText: Counted against the live cart, not against a single request, so a model cannot get around it by adding one at a time. Leave at 0 unless you have a reason — it is the shopper's own cart, and your checkout still decides what is a real order.

input-field.name: maxCartValue
input-field.label: Highest cart total the assistant may reach
input-field.helpText: In your sales channel's currency, checked against the live cart total. Worth leaving at 0 unless your catalogue makes a ceiling meaningful — one expensive product is enough to make a number chosen here block a genuine sale.

input-field.name: maxToolCallsPerTurn
input-field.label: Most lookups the assistant may make per reply
input-field.helpText: The one limit that cannot be switched off, because it is what stops a model that has started looping. Reaching it ends the reply gracefully with whatever was already found, never with an error. A single question can easily use several lookups — a search, a stock check, an add to cart — so lower this only if you are watching costs closely. Blank or 0 falls back to 20.

card.name: requestLimits
card.title: Request limits
card.subtitle: Your chat page is public and every message costs you model credit. Only the per-shopper limit is on by default.

input-field.name: requestsPerMinute
input-field.label: Messages per minute, per shopper
input-field.helpText: This is the one control that stops a script hammering your shop, which is why it ships on. 60 is roughly twenty times what a person typing can produce, so real shoppers never meet it. Counted per visitor in a rolling window; someone over the limit is turned away before your shop reads or writes anything. 0 removes the limit.

input-field.name: dailyRequestCap
input-field.label: Messages per day, whole sales channel
input-field.helpText: A spending ceiling, off by default. Set one only if you want the assistant to stop for the day at a known number — and note that when it trips, every shopper gets nothing until it resets, including the ones who would have bought something. The 24 hours start at the first message of the day, not at midnight, and clearing your shop's cache resets the count.

input-field.name: entryPointStyle
input-field.label: Entry point

option.name: Chat icon — neutral, takes your colours

input-field.helpText: Both take your colours. The chat icon is a flat mark that holds still, and while the assistant is thinking it shows three quiet dots. The character is a shaded sphere that floats, blinks, follows the pointer and changes expression as the conversation goes — more personality than most shops want, and unmistakable when you do.

input-field.name: primaryColor
input-field.label: Primary colour
input-field.helpText: The action colour: the entry point, the send button, focus outlines. Left empty, the shipped blue is used. Text on top of it is chosen for you so it stays readable — a pale colour gets dark text, not white.

input-field.name: secondaryColor
input-field.label: Secondary colour
input-field.helpText: The quiet surface behind the assistant's replies. Deliberately not a second action colour: if two things on screen shout equally loudly, a shopper cannot tell which one is the button.

input-field.name: enableEscalation
input-field.label: Let the assistant hand a conversation to a human
input-field.helpText: When off, the handover tool is never built, so the model cannot see it and cannot call it. The assistant then simply says it cannot answer, without offering anywhere to go.

input-field.name: escalationUrl
input-field.label: Where shoppers reach a human
input-field.helpText: A page on this shop (/contact) or a full https address. Leave it empty and the assistant says it cannot help instead of offering a link — it will never suggest someone will follow up when there is nowhere to send them. Only http and https addresses are accepted, because this link is shown to every shopper.

input-field.name: escalationMessage
input-field.label: Handover message
input-field.placeholder: Our team can help with orders, returns and anything account-related.
input-field.helpText: Shown above the link when the assistant hands over. Say what your team can actually help with. Left empty, a translated default is used.

input-field.name: assistantName
input-field.label: Assistant name
input-field.helpText: Shown in the panel heading, and read out by screen readers. Defaults to "Shopping Assistant".

input-field.name: greeting
input-field.label: Greeting
input-field.placeholder: Welcome to our shop! I can look up products, prices and availability — what are you after?
input-field.helpText: The first message a shopper sees. Say what the assistant can look up, not how clever it is. Left empty, a translated default is used.

card.name: logging
card.title: Logging
card.subtitle: Separate from the conversation list in Settings, which records every conversation in full and is always on.

input-field.name: logTraces
input-field.label: Log a line for every reply
input-field.helpText: Writes one line to your shop's log each time the assistant replies: which sales channel, how the reply ended and how long it took. Useful for spotting failures and slow replies without opening conversations one by one. No shopper messages are ever written to the log — a log file does not have the deletion schedule or the access rules that the conversation list has.

input-field.name: traceRetentionDays
input-field.label: Keep conversations for (days)
input-field.helpText: Conversations older than this are deleted every day, along with their records. There is deliberately no "keep forever": these rows hold what shoppers typed, so a table that only grows is a data-protection problem rather than a convenience. Blank or 0 falls back to 30 days.
